headline: 00 scan) -- Saudi coalition intercepts TWO Ansar Allah ballistic missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu
dek: The coalition intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by Yemen's Ansar Allah towards the Saudi cities of Taif and Yanbu on Saturday morning. Saudi Civil Defence briefly issued alerts for Jeddah, Yanbu, Taif and Mecca, then announced the danger had passed ~10 minutes later.
sources: Saudi-led coalition spokesman Brig-Gen Turki al-Maliki, X post, via Saudi Press Agency (SPA); Saudi Civil Defence alerts
fault_line: Yanbu is the bypass that was supposed to make Hormuz survivable — if the Ansar Allah can reach the bypass itself, what route is safe?

sections.what_happened: The coalition intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by Yemen's Ansar Allah towards the Saudi cities of Taif and Yanbu on Saturday morning. Saudi Civil Defence briefly issued alerts for Jeddah, Yanbu, Taif and Mecca, then announced the danger had passed ~10 minutes later. This follows the early-Saturday Riyadh missile intercept and Eastern Province drone intercept already recorded (totw-20261024-0700-01/0800-03). Yanbu is a major Red Sea oil-export hub that has allowed Riyadh to bypass Iran's Hormuz blockade for much of its crude exports (Dawn/AFP, Dhaka Tribune). No casualties or damage reported from the Taif/Yanbu intercepts.
sections.what_verified: Coalition statement carried by AFP (T1, via Dawn/LBC), Reuters (T1, via Times of Israel liveblog/Hathalyoum), Al Jazeera liveblog (T2, STATE-QA), Anadolu (T3, STATE-TR, via APA), Gulf News liveblog. The interception itself is the coalition's claim; no independent debris/damage confirmation in this window.
sections.what_disputed: No Ansar Allah claim of the Taif/Yanbu launches surfaced in this window; launch attribution rests on the coalition. No independent verification of interception success beyond coalition channels. The Riyadh airport strike earlier in October (13 killed per Dhaka Tribune) shows not all launches are intercepted.
sections.why_matters: The bypass is now a target: two missiles aimed at Yanbu, the Red Sea port that lets Saudi oil dodge Hormuz — intercepted, but the message landed. Follow the bypass, not just the Strait.
sections.context: Background: NEW to scans (big-missed; event Sat morning Oct 24, missed by the 14:00 scan) -- Saudi coalition intercepts TWO Ansar Allah ballistic missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu; civil-defence alerts briefly covered Mecca, Jeddah, Taif, Yanbu

totw_analysis: Our read: The bypass is now a target: two missiles aimed at Yanbu, the Red Sea port that lets Saudi oil dodge Hormuz — intercepted, but the message landed. Follow the bypass, not just the Strait. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Yanbu is the bypass that was supposed to make Hormuz survivable — if the Ansar Allah can reach the bypass itself, what route is safe?
